title: Gate every vCenter data source creation on its VCF Operations for Networks precheck
prompt:
Implement src/vcfon_vcenter/client.py and src/vcfon_vcenter/onboarding.py in this stdlib-only Python package, which registers a batch of vCenter data sources with a VCF Operations for Networks 9.1 appliance. Both files are stubs today; transport.py, plan.py and errors.py are already written and should be used as they are. docs/contract.json is the local REST contract for the four operations involved (create, validateVCenter, addVcenterDatasource, delete) and docs/official_sources.json records its provenance; the contract is authoritative for method, path, payload shape and success status. README.md states the required run order and the exact report dict that onboard_vcenters must return.

Registering a data source is a mutation an operator has to undo by hand, so every vCenter gets its precheck first and the precheck gates the creation. Obtain a token with create, then for each plan datasource in plan order call validateVCenter and, only if that precheck passed, call addVcenterDatasource for the same vCenter. A precheck passes only when validateVCenter answered HTTP 200 and the BaseDataSourceValidationResponse body's own code is 200: the appliance answers HTTP 200 carrying a body code such as 401 when the request was well formed but the verdict is negative, so the HTTP status alone is not the verdict. When a precheck does not pass, addVcenterDatasource for that vCenter must not be sent at all -- not sent and its result ignored, not sent. One vCenter's outcome never stops the next, and the token is released with delete whether or not anything failed.

Encode requests exactly as the contract specifies. The Authorization header is 'NetworkInsight {token}' on every operation except create, which must send none because the spec declares security: [] on it. Exactly one of ip and fqdn appears in a data source body; the other is absent. An optional field the operator did not set must be absent from the JSON object rather than sent as null, an empty string, zero or an empty object -- that covers notes, is_vmc and ipfix_request on a create, ipfix_enabled on a validate, value inside a Domain, and the domain object itself. An enabled the operator set to false is set, not unset, so it must appear as the JSON literal false even though its spec default is true. Inside ipfix_request only the keys the operator actually set appear. VCenterDataSourceValidationRequest is a strictly smaller schema than VCenterDataSourceRequest -- its only members are ip, fqdn, proxy_id, credentials and ipfix_enabled -- so nickname, notes, enabled, is_vmc and ipfix_request must never reach the validate operation, and the IPFIX intent that a create spells as the ipfix_request object is spelled on a validate as the flat ipfix_enabled boolean. delete sends no request body.

Run python3 tests/verify.py. Only src/vcfon_vcenter/client.py and src/vcfon_vcenter/onboarding.py are implementation files; docs/, fixtures/, tests/, README.md and the other modules under src/vcfon_vcenter/ are protected fixtures and must not be changed.
scenario: validateVCenter is the precheck for addVcenterDatasource, its verdict lives in the response body's own code rather than the HTTP status, and a failed verdict must leave the appliance untouched for that vCenter
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves the gate held, that the validate body carries only the smaller validation schema's members, and that every unset optional field was omitted rather than sent empty
